# get_time_interval

## Description

This function determines the time interval (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, yearly) of a dataset based on the differences between the first two time points.

```r
get_time_interval(data, time, unit = NULL, area = NULL)
```

## Arguments

- `data`: an object of class 'data.frame' containing equally spaced time series data (daily, weekly, monthly data) for one or multiple spatial units.
- `time`: A string representing the name of the column in `data` that contains time information. The column should be in "yyyy-mm-dd" format.
- `unit`: (Optional) A string representing the names of the columns in `data` that identifies the different units for which a time series is available, typically a spatial unit. Required if `data` contains multiple units.
- `area`: Deprecated, use `unit` instead.

## Returns

A character string indicating the time interval of the dataset. Possible values: "day", "week", "month", "year", or "unknown".

## Examples

```r
df <- data.frame(
  date = seq(as.Date("2020-01-01"), by = "week", length.out = 10),
  cases = 1:10
)
get_time_interval(df, time = "date")
```
